name: Loop Engineering Prompts
description: ループ工学の教材プロンプト集＋Ralph原典（日本語訳付き）

loops.title: Daily triage (report-only)
loops.titleJa: 日次トリアージ（報告のみ）
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: the heartbeat in its safest form. Discover and report, change nothing.
loops.descriptionJa: プロジェクトを日次で調べ、STATE.md に高優先度・監視対象・ノイズを追記する。まず報告だけさせ、自動修正はしない安全な第一段階。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
Run $loop-triage on this project. Read STATE.md if present.

Append to STATE.md:
- High-Priority Items → "## High Priority" section
- Watch Items → "## Watch List"
- Update "Last run" timestamp

Week 1: report only. Do not modify source files.

Flag anything ambiguous for the Triage inbox.

loops.title: Issue triage (propose-only, quantified)
loops.titleJa: Issueトリアージ（定量・提案のみ）
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: note the count + delta each run (queue health over time) and the explicit needs-human bucket.
loops.descriptionJa: Issueを定量的に評価して分類し、提案のみを状態ファイルに記録する。勝手に変更しない。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
Run $issue-triage on this project. Read issue-triage-state.md if present.

Update issue-triage-state.md:
- Last run timestamp
- Open actionable count + delta since last run
- Top 5 prioritized issues with one-sentence summaries
- Suggested labels (proposed only — do not apply)
- "needs human" bucket for ambiguous, duplicate, or security-sensitive items

Week 1: report only. Do not modify issues, labels, or source files.
Flag anything touching auth, payments, or public API for human review.

loops.title: PR babysitter (attempt-capped, propose-never-merge)
loops.titleJa: PRお守り（試行上限・マージ禁止）
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: a capped fix loop with a mandatory verifier APPROVE gate and a hard "propose, never merge" rule.
loops.descriptionJa: オープンPRをレビュー・トリアージするが、試行回数に上限を設け、マージは決して行わず提案に留める。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
For open PRs on this repo (team-authored or label loop-watch):

1. Run $pr-review-triage
2. Update pr-babysitter-state.md
3. If CI red or actionable review comment AND attempts < 3:
   - Open worktree
   - Implementer: $minimal-fix
   - Verifier subagent: must APPROVE
   - Comment on PR with proposal — do not merge
4. If attempts >= 3 or high-risk labels: Triage inbox + escalate

loops.title: CI repair (event-triggered, full contract)
loops.titleJa: CI修復（イベント起動・契約付き）
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: event trigger plus a nightly backup sweep; one hypothesis per run; the exit code is the only success signal; scope creep is named as the main failure mode.
loops.descriptionJa: 必須チェックが失敗したときに起動し、契約（目的・トリガー・検証・停止条件）に沿ってCIを修復する。夜間の一括処理も行う。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
Automation: CI repair triage
Trigger: when a required check fails on an open PR (and a nightly sweep as backup).
Workspace: isolated worktree off the PR branch.

Task:
1. Reproduce the failing check. Identify the exact failing command or the closest local equivalent.
2. Read the failing logs and the changed files. Form one hypothesis about the cause.
3. If the cause is mechanical and in scope, patch only that cause in the worktree.
4. Rerun the failing command first. Treat its exit code as the only signal of success.
5. Record the failing log excerpt, the patch, and the passing output in a PR comment.

Permission boundary:
- Edit only the files implicated by the failure.
- Do not change CI config, upgrade dependencies, or edit unrelated files.
- Do not merge, force-push, or alter required checks.

Stop conditions:
- Stop when the failing command passes and the diff is scoped to the cause.
- Stop after 3 repair attempts.
- Stop if the failure is outside scope (flaky infra, test design, missing service).

Escalation:
- If stopped without success, post a PR comment summarizing the failing command,
  what was tried, and why it is out of scope, then request a human reviewer.

loops.title: Morning digest (idempotent, miss-tolerant scheduled task)
loops.titleJa: 朝のダイジェスト（冪等・欠落耐性）
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: idempotent scheduled work driven by a last-run marker. Fail visibly, not silently instead of emitting an empty artifact. ---
loops.descriptionJa: 平日8:30にリポジトリの状況ダイジェストを生成する。実行が飛んでも破綻しない冪等な設計。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
Schedule: weekdays at 08:30 local time.

Objective: produce a morning status digest for this repository.

Each run:
1. In a fresh worktree off the default branch, collect: open PRs needing review,
   failing checks on main, and issues labeled "urgent" opened since the last run.
2. Verify each item against live GitHub state before including it.
3. Write the digest to reports/morning-digest-<date>.md with one source link per item.
4. Record the last-run timestamp in reports/.digest-state so the next run only adds new items.

Permission boundary:
- Read GitHub state and write only under reports/.
- Do not modify code, comment on PRs, or change issue state.

Escalation:
- If GitHub is unreachable, write a short "digest skipped: <reason>" note and exit
  rather than producing an empty or stale digest.

loops.title: The textbook stop condition
loops.titleJa: 教科書的な停止条件
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Source: the /goal primitive and this exact example are documented in Addy Osmani, "Loop Engineering" (June 7, 2026), where he notes both Claude Code and Codex ship /goal. — /goal keeps working turn after turn until a verifier confirms the condition. The condition must be verifiable — an exit code, a test result — not a vibe.
loops.descriptionJa: テストが通りlintがクリーンになるまで実行する、最も基本的な /goal。停止条件は「感覚」ではなく終了コードで判定できるものにする。
loops.kickoffPrompt: /goal All tests in test/auth pass and lint is clean

loops.title: A scope-bounded /goal
loops.titleJa: スコープ限定の /goal
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Pattern: bake the scope limit into the goal itself, so "done" also means "didn't sprawl." ---
loops.descriptionJa: 完了条件そのものに「差分が指定ディレクトリ配下のみ」という範囲制限を埋め込み、実装の暴走を防ぐ。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
/goal All tests in test/auth/ pass, lint is clean, and the diff touches only
files under src/auth/ and test/auth/.

loops.title: Stage 1: report-only (start every new loop here)
loops.titleJa: 段階1：報告のみのループ
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: run a new unattended loop in pure report-only mode for a week before you grant it write access. Earn trust before granting autonomy.
loops.descriptionJa: 新しいループは必ずここから始める。調査して STATE.md にまとめるだけで、コードは変更しない。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
/loop 1d Run $loop-triage. Read STATE.md. Merge findings into High Priority and
Watch List. Update Last run. Do not edit code.

loops.title: Stage 2: small auto-fixes, with isolation + a verifier
loops.titleJa: 段階2：小さな自動修正＋検証者
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: graduating autonomy (L1 → L2) means worktree isolation plus a separate verifier sub-agent before any auto-fix.
loops.descriptionJa: 単一ファイルのバグ修正に限って実装エージェントを起動し、隔離環境と検証者を伴って自動修正する。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
/loop 1d Run $loop-triage. For high-priority items that are single-file bugfixes:
spawn an implementer in a worktree, then a verifier agent. Update STATE.md.
Escalate ambiguous items.

loops.title: A full daily-triage /loop (skill + worktree + reviewer + connectors)
loops.titleJa: 日次トリアージ（フル構成）
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: one /loop line wiring together every building block: skill → worktree → minimal-fix → reviewer → connectors → escalation.
loops.descriptionJa: スキル・ワークツリー・レビュアー・コネクタを組み合わせた本格的な日次トリアージループ。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
/loop 1d Run the loop-triage skill on the current project. Append high-priority
items to STATE.md. For any small, self-contained bugfix or CI failure, open an
isolated worktree, draft a minimal fix using the minimal-fix skill, and have a
reviewer sub-agent verify it against project skills and tests. Update the PR or
ticket via connectors if possible. Anything ambiguous or high-risk should be
clearly flagged for human review in STATE.md.

loops.title: A complete session-scoped /loop contract
loops.titleJa: セッション単位のループ契約
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: this is the gold standard for a session-scoped loop. A deterministic exit code as the only "done" signal, an explicit permission boundary, an iteration budget, an anti-cheat clause, and a stall stop. Copy it.
loops.descriptionJa: 15分ごとにテストの緑を保つ。各反復で実行する手順・検証・停止条件を契約として明記した完全な形。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
/loop every 15m

Objective: keep `npm test` green on the current branch.

Each iteration:
1. Run `npm test`. Treat its exit code as the only signal of done.
2. If it passes, stop and say the loop is complete.
3. If it fails, read the last 80 lines of output and fix only the cause of that failure.
4. Append one line to LOOP_PROGRESS.md describing what you changed and why.
5. Read LOOP_PROGRESS.md at the start of each iteration so you do not repeat a failed fix.

Permission boundary:
- Edit only application and test files under src/ and tests/.
- Do not change CI config, add dependencies, or touch files outside this repo.
- Do not weaken or delete tests to make them pass.

Stop conditions:
- Stop when `npm test` passes.
- Stop after 5 iterations.
- Stop if the same failure repeats twice with no new evidence.

loops.title: High-frequency cadence loops bound to skills
loops.titleJa: 高頻度ケイデンス（スキル連動）
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: The everyday shape: short-cadence loops bound to slash-command skills. ⚠️ Treat the precise /loop 5m … wording as illustrative, not a verbatim quote. Boris Cherny's verified line is that he writes loops, not these exact cadence strings. ---
loops.descriptionJa: 5分ごとのPR監視、30分ごとのフィードバック収集など、短い間隔でスキルに紐づけて回す。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
/loop 5m  /pr-babysit check
/loop 30m /slack-feedback

loops.title: The contract shape
loops.titleJa: ループ契約のJSON雛形
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Every contract answers the same questions: If one is missing, the loop becomes either a manual prompting habit or an unsafe background automation. The skeleton: ---
loops.descriptionJa: goal / when / pick_work / sandbox / checks / memory / limits / hand_off を定義する契約の骨格。すべてのループはこの形に落とせる。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
{
  "loop":      "<short name>",
  "goal":      "<the one verifiable thing 'done' means>",
  "when":      { "on": "schedule | event", "fires": "<cadence or event>" },
  "pick_work": "<what this loop may act on, and nothing else>",
  "sandbox":   { "where": "<isolation>", "never": ["<off-limits action>"] },
  "checks":    ["<a gate the work must pass>"],
  "memory":    "<what persists between runs, and where>",
  "limits":    { "max_turns": 0, "max_minutes": 0 },
  "hand_off":  { "when": ["<escalation trigger>"], "to": "<who or where>" },
  "done":      { "success": "<finished well>", "give_up": "<stopped without success>" }
}

loops.title: PR babysitter
loops.titleJa: 契約：PRお守り
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: act only on explicit blockers; propose, never merge; escalate on the second repeat of the same failure.
loops.descriptionJa: 人が張り付かずに1つのPRをマージ可能へ進める契約。作業の選び方・砂場・検査・記憶・上限・引き渡しを明記する。

loops.title: CI repair
loops.titleJa: 契約：CI修復
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: distinguish real regressions from flakes; the original failing command passing is the only success gate.
loops.descriptionJa: 失敗したCIシグナルを、小さな検証済み修正か的確なエスカレーションに変える契約。

loops.title: Incident response (read-only, diagnose-only)
loops.titleJa: 契約：インシデント対応（読取専用・診断のみ）
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: some loops should be forbidden from acting. This one correlates evidence and pages a human, but can never touch production. Note the gate: "missing telemetry is reported as unknown, never healthy."
loops.descriptionJa: 新規アラートを証拠に基づくトリアージ済みインシデントに変える。読み取り専用で、修正はしない。

loops.title: Dependency triage (risk-bucketed)
loops.titleJa: 契約：依存トリアージ（リスク別）
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: automate only the "safe patch" bucket; defer everything riskier with reasons.
loops.descriptionJa: 依存更新を、安全なパッチ・保留・人的レビューの3バケツに仕分ける契約。

loops.title: PR review (read-only, comment-only)
loops.titleJa: 契約：PRレビュー（読取専用・コメントのみ）
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: comment, never approve. Heterogeneity is the point — a reviewer that is a different agent than the maker catches what self-review can't. (See docs/05 and the four-reviewer case study in docs/11.)
loops.descriptionJa: オープンされた全PRに、証拠に基づく実質的な初回レビューを付ける。変更はせずコメントのみ。

loops.title: Documentation-drift repair
loops.titleJa: 契約：ドキュメント乖離の修復
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: the loop fixes mechanical drift (a renamed symbol, a dead link) and escalates intent — it must never invent behavior to make a doc "true."
loops.descriptionJa: 改名・削除されたAPIへの参照など、コードとドキュメントの乖離を検知して直す契約。

loops.title: Flaky-test hunt
loops.titleJa: 契約：フレーキーテスト狩り
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: the danger is a maker that "fixes" flakiness by deleting the test or adding a retry. The gate is strict — a flake must be proven (pass and fail on one commit), and a deterministic failure is escalated as a bug, never masked. ---
loops.descriptionJa: 同一コミットで成功も失敗もする本当にフレーキーなテストを特定し、方針に沿って隔離する契約。

loops.title: A portable shell-cron loop (gate-first)
loops.titleJa: シェル/cronループ（ゲート優先）
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: When you don't have a hosted automations tab, a cron + a "gate before acting" script is enough: Why this shape: gate before acting (skip if already green), a lock dir to prevent overlapping runs, and receipts in a log file. ---
loops.descriptionJa: まず検査を実行し、既に通っていれば何もしない。無駄な実行を避ける移植性の高いシェルループ。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
# Gate first: if the check already passes, there is no work to do.
if bash -c "$CHECK_CMD" >/tmp/loop-check.out 2>&1; then
  echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) ok: check already green" >> "$RECEIPTS"; exit 0
fi

prompt="The check '$CHECK_CMD' is failing. Latest output:
$(tail -n 80 /tmp/loop-check.out)

Fix only the cause of this failure. Do not change CI config, add dependencies,
or edit unrelated files. Append one line to loop-receipts.log describing the change."

$AGENT_CMD "$prompt"

# Re-gate: the deterministic check, not the agent, decides success.

loops.title: A portable shell-cron loop (gate-first)
loops.titleJa: Ralph：技法を1行で
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: When you don't have a hosted automations tab, a cron + a "gate before acting" script is enough: Why this shape: gate before acting (skip if already green), a lock dir to prevent overlapping runs, and receipts in a log file. ---
loops.descriptionJa: PROMPT.md を延々とエージェントに流し込むだけ、というRalph技法の本質。最小にして原型。
loops.kickoffPrompt: 0 9 * * 1-5 cd /path/to/repo && CHECK_CMD="npm test" AGENT_CMD="claude -p" ./loop-wrapper.sh

loops.title: 1. The whole technique in one line
loops.titleJa: Ralph：1ターンに1つだけ
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Source: Geoffrey Huntley, ghuntley.com/ralph. — Ralph in its purest form: a bare loop feeding one prompt to a fresh agent forever. "Deterministically bad in an undeterministic world" — crude, but it works because each turn re-reads the plan from disk. The loop is agent-agnostic — the same shape drives any headless CLI agent: Source: Ian Nuttall, iannuttall/ralph.
loops.descriptionJa: 計画から最重要の1件を選び、変更前にコードベースを検索し、そのうえで1つだけ実装する中核指示。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
# pick your runner — Ralph doesn't care which
AGENT_CMD="claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions \"$(cat PROMPT.md)\""
AGENT_CMD="codex exec --yolo -"
AGENT_CMD="opencode run \"$(cat PROMPT.md)\""
AGENT_CMD="droid exec --skip-permissions-unsafe -f PROMPT.md"

loops.title: 2. The core loop instruction: do ONE thing per turn
loops.titleJa: Ralph：変更した単位をテストする（背圧）
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Source: Geoffrey Huntley, ghuntley.com/ralph. — Two lessons in three lines: do exactly one thing per loop (let the model pick which), and search before building so the amnesiac agent doesn't re-implement code that already exists (Ralph's "Achilles' heel").
loops.descriptionJa: 実装や修正の直後に、その単位のテストを実行させる。ループに背圧をかけて暴走を防ぐ。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
Follow @fix_plan.md and choose the most important thing.
Before making changes search codebase (don't assume not implemented)
using parallel subagents. Think hard.

loops.title: 3. Test the unit you just changed (backpressure)
loops.titleJa: Ralph：仮実装の禁止標識
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Source: Geoffrey Huntley, ghuntley.com/ralph. — Immediate, scoped verification after each change is the wheel that has to turn fast.
loops.descriptionJa: プレースホルダや手抜き実装を禁じる強い標識。完全な実装だけを受け入れる。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
After implementing functionality or resolving problems, run the tests for that
unit of code that was improved. If functionality is missing then it's your job
to add it as per the application specifications. Think hard.

If tests unrelated to your work fail then it's your job to resolve these tests
as part of the increment of change.

loops.title: 4. The anti-placeholder "sign"
loops.titleJa: Ralph：ループに学習させる
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Source: Geoffrey Huntley, ghuntley.com/ralph. — Models chase the reward (compiling code) and will happily stub. Huntley uses loud, escalating-number "signs" to counter the placeholder bias. (Yes, it's silly. Yes, it works.)
loops.descriptionJa: ビルド方法など運用上の学びを見つけたら AGENT.md を更新させ、次の反復に引き継ぐ。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
9999999999999999999999999999. DO NOT IMPLEMENT PLACEHOLDER OR SIMPLE
IMPLEMENTATIONS. WE WANT FULL IMPLEMENTATIONS. DO IT OR I WILL YELL AT YOU

loops.title: 6. A complete, generic PROMPT.md (the everyday Ralph contract)
loops.titleJa: Ralph：汎用PROMPT.md（日常版）
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Source: RepoMirror, repomirrorhq/repomirror. — The minimal generic Ralph contract: orient → single highest-priority item → verify → update plan + commit. The spec is the source of truth.
loops.descriptionJa: 仕様を読み、最優先の1件を選び、実装し、テストし、記録する。そのまま使える完全なRalph契約。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
0a. read everything in specs/
0b. review the files in src/

1. pick the SINGLE highest priority item from @IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and
   implement it using up to 50 subagents
2. ensure the tests and checks are passing
3. update the @IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md with your progress and commit all changes
   with git add -A && git commit -m "..."

if there is a discrepancy in the IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and the spec, always
update the IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md to match the spec.

loops.title: 7. The "two prompts" pattern: a separate PLAN prompt
loops.titleJa: Ralph：計画と実装を分ける2プロンプト
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Ralph practitioners keep a disposable planning prompt that only does gap analysis (specs vs. code) and rewrites the plan — it implements nothing: Source: Clayton Farr, ClaytonFarr/ralph-playbook (condensed). — Separating "plan" from "build" keeps each loop turn focused and the plan honest.
loops.descriptionJa: 実装計画を精査する専用プロンプトと、実装するプロンプトを分離するパターン。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
Study @IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md (it may be incorrect) and use up to 500 subagents
to study existing source code in src/ and compare it against specs/. Create or
update @IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md as a bullet-point list sorted by priority of items
yet to be implemented. Consider searching for TODO, minimal implementations,
placeholders, skipped/flaky tests, and inconsistent patterns.

IMPORTANT: Plan only. Do NOT implement anything. Do NOT assume functionality is
missing; confirm with a code search first.

loops.title: 9. Give the loop a real stop signal
loops.titleJa: Ralph：本物の停止信号を与える
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: The bare while :; loop never stops on its own. Production Ralphs add an explicit, machine-detectable exit: Source: Ryan Carson, snarktank/ralph. Source: Frank Bria, frankbria/ralph-claude-code. — A dual gate guards against the agent sounding done without being done.
loops.descriptionJa: 全ストーリーが passes: true になったら完了マーカーを出力させ、ループを確実に終わらせる。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
When all stories have `passes: true`, output <promise>COMPLETE</promise> and the
loop exits.

loops.title: 10. A production loop wrapper (mode + iteration cap + push)
loops.titleJa: Ralph：本番用ループラッパー
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Source: Clayton Farr, ClaytonFarr/ralph-playbook. — A hard iteration cap is the cheapest budget guardrail there is. Always set one. ---
loops.descriptionJa: モード指定・反復上限・自動pushを備えた、実運用向けのシェルラッパー。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
#!/bin/bash
# Usage: ./loop.sh [plan|build] [max_iterations]
ITERATION=0
while true; do
    if [ "$MAX_ITERATIONS" -gt 0 ] && [ "$ITERATION" -ge "$MAX_ITERATIONS" ]; then
        echo "Reached max iterations: $MAX_ITERATIONS"; break
    fi
    cat "$PROMPT_FILE" | claude -p \
        --dangerously-skip-permissions \
        --output-format=stream-json \
        --model opus --verbose
    git push origin "$CURRENT_BRANCH" || git push -u origin "$CURRENT_BRANCH"
    ITERATION=$((ITERATION + 1))
done

loops.title: Run the checker on a stronger model (Codex sub-agent)
loops.titleJa: 検証者を上位モデルで動かす
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: a common pattern. The maker runs on a fast, cheap model; the checker runs on the strongest model at high reasoning effort, read-only.
loops.descriptionJa: 検証者を別プロセス・別モデルとして定義し、条件を満たさない修正を却下させる。生成と評価の分離。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
# .codex/agents/verifier.toml
name = "verifier"
description = "Rejects loop fixes unless tests pass and scope is minimal"
instructions = "See loop-verifier SKILL above."
model = "strongest-available"
reasoning_effort = "high"
read_only = true

loops.title: The four-role durable loop: PLANNER → IMPLEMENTOR → REVIEWER → JUDGE
loops.titleJa: 4役の永続ループ
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Adapted from Joel Hooks' joelclaw agent-loop skill. The killer detail: the reviewer writes tests from the acceptance criteria without reading the implementation, so it can't rubber-stamp the maker. ---
loops.descriptionJa: PLANNER → IMPLEMENTOR → REVIEWER → 記録 の4役で回す、状態が持続するループ構成。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
loop start
  → PLANNER reads prd.json, finds the next unpassed story
    → IMPLEMENTOR makes changes, commits
      → REVIEWER writes tests from the acceptance criteria
                 (independently — does NOT read the implementation)
        → JUDGE: all green? → mark story passed, go to next
                 failing?   → retry with feedback (up to maxRetries)
                 exhausted? → skip, flag for human review, go to next

Rules:
- Acceptance criteria must be machine-verifiable (tests, typecheck, lint).
- `passes` flips to true only when the JUDGE approves.
- `skipped: true` is added on max-retry exhaustion (never silently dropped).

loops.title: A binary PASS/FAIL grader (the simplest useful shape)
loops.titleJa: PASS/FAIL の二値判定者
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Source: pattern from Clayton Farr, ClaytonFarr/ralph-playbook ("non-deterministic backpressure"). — Turns a subjective acceptance criterion into a binary gate a loop can iterate against. Usage in a test:
loops.descriptionJa: 観測可能な基準1つに対して合否のみを返す、最も単純で有用な判定者。曖昧な評価を排除する。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
You are a strict reviewer. Evaluate the ARTIFACT against the CRITERIA.

CRITERIA: <one observable, behavioral criterion>
ARTIFACT: <text, or a screenshot path>

Return JSON only:
{ "pass": <true|false>, "feedback": "<only when pass=false: the single most
  important reason, specific and actionable>" }

Rules:
- Judge only against the stated criterion. Do not invent new requirements.
- If you cannot tell from the artifact, return pass=false with feedback asking
  for the missing evidence.

loops.title: An evaluation-regression judge (grounded in traces)
loops.titleJa: 評価リグレッションの判定者
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: the judge must ground every verdict in trace evidence plus run IDs, and is explicitly forbidden from "changing scorers to make failures disappear."
loops.descriptionJa: 失敗トレースを直近の正常時と比較し、劣化の原因を証拠に基づいて特定する。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
Investigate evaluation regression <run id>.
Compare failing traces against the last known-good baseline.
Classify the likely cause BEFORE editing.
Patch only the smallest prompt, context, harness, scorer, or fixture issue
supported by trace evidence.
Rerun targeted evals, record run IDs and score deltas, and escalate if the fix
risks overfitting.

Verification gates:
- Targeted failing tasks improve or return to baseline.
- No known sentinel tasks regress.
- Trace evidence supports the claimed cause.
- Score changes are reported with sample size, variance caveat, and run IDs.

loops.title: A security-review judge (read-only, evidence-gated)
loops.titleJa: セキュリティレビュー判定者
loops.author: awesome-loop-engineering
loops.description: Why this shape: a grader that must distinguish "exploitable" from "speculative" with repository-specific evidence; default read-only. ---
loops.descriptionJa: PR・ブランチ・リリースに対し、読み取り専用でセキュリティレビューを行う。狭い修正以外は変更しない。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
Run a security review loop for <PR, branch, or release>.
Stay read-only unless a narrow mechanical fix is explicitly safe.
Map the changed attack surface, run allowed checks, validate each finding with
evidence, and avoid speculative claims.
Report impact, evidence, recommended fix, residual risk, and escalation needs.
Do not access production secrets or perform destructive testing.

Gates:
- Findings cite concrete files, paths, inputs, commands, or traces.
- Static analysis or tests support the claim when possible.
- Suggested fixes do not weaken security controls or broaden permissions.

loops.title: Ralph Agent Instructions (original)
loops.titleJa: Ralph 原典プロンプト
loops.author: snarktank/ralph
loops.description: Ralph is an autonomous AI agent loop that runs repeatedly until all PRD items are complete.
loops.descriptionJa: PRD(prd.json)の全項目が完了するまで反復する自律エージェントループの原典。優先度最上位の未完ストーリーを1つ選んで実装し、品質チェックを通し、コミットし、進捗と学びを追記する。
loops.kickoffPrompt:
# Ralph Agent Instructions

You are an autonomous coding agent working on a software project.

## Your Task

1. Read the PRD at `prd.json` (in the same directory as this file)
2. Read the progress log at `progress.txt` (check Codebase Patterns section first)
3. Check you're on the correct branch from PRD `branchName`. If not, check it out or create from main.
4. Pick the **highest priority** user story where `passes: false`
5. Implement that single user story
6. Run quality checks (e.g., typecheck, lint, test - use whatever your project requires)
7. Update AGENTS.md files if you discover reusable patterns (see below)
8. If checks pass, commit ALL changes with message: `feat: [Story ID] - [Story Title]`
9. Update the PRD to set `passes: true` for the completed story
10. Append your progress to `progress.txt`

## Progress Report Format

APPEND to progress.txt (never replace, always append):
```
## [Date/Time] - [Story ID]
Thread: https://ampcode.com/threads/$AMP_CURRENT_THREAD_ID
- What was implemented
- Files changed
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Patterns discovered (e.g., "this codebase uses X for Y")
  - Gotchas encountered (e.g., "don't forget to update Z when changing W")
  - Useful context (e.g., "the evaluation panel is in component X")
---
```

Include the thread URL so future iterations can use the `read_thread` tool to reference previous work if needed.

The learnings section is critical - it helps future iterations avoid repeating mistakes and understand the codebase better.

## Consolidate Patterns

If you discover a **reusable pattern** that future iterations should know, add it to the `## Codebase Patterns` section at the TOP of progress.txt (create it if it doesn't exist). This section should consolidate the most important learnings:

```
## Codebase Patterns
- Example: Use `sql<number>` template for aggregations
- Example: Always use `IF NOT EXISTS` for migrations
- Example: Export types from actions.ts for UI components
```

Only add patterns that are **general and reusable**, not story-specific details.

## Update AGENTS.md Files

Before committing, check if any edited files have learnings worth preserving in nearby AGENTS.md files:

1. **Identify directories with edited files** - Look at which directories you modified
2. **Check for existing AGENTS.md** - Look for AGENTS.md in those directories or parent directories
3. **Add valuable learnings** - If you discovered something future developers/agents should know:
   - API patterns or conventions specific to that module
   - Gotchas or non-obvious requirements
   - Dependencies between files
   - Testing approaches for that area
   - Configuration or environment requirements

**Examples of good AGENTS.md additions:**
- "When modifying X, also update Y to keep them in sync"
- "This module uses pattern Z for all API calls"
- "Tests require the dev server running on PORT 3000"
- "Field names must match the template exactly"

**Do NOT add:**
- Story-specific implementation details
- Temporary debugging notes
- Information already in progress.txt

Only update AGENTS.md if you have **genuinely reusable knowledge** that would help future work in that directory.

## Quality Requirements

- ALL commits must pass your project's quality checks (typecheck, lint, test)
- Do NOT commit broken code
- Keep changes focused and minimal
- Follow existing code patterns

## Browser Testing (Required for Frontend Stories)

For any story that changes UI, you MUST verify it works in the browser:

1. Load the `dev-browser` skill
2. Navigate to the relevant page
3. Verify the UI changes work as expected
4. Take a screenshot if helpful for the progress log

A frontend story is NOT complete until browser verification passes.

## Stop Condition

After completing a user story, check if ALL stories have `passes: true`.

If ALL stories are complete and passing, reply with:
<promise>COMPLETE</promise>

If there are still stories with `passes: false`, end your response normally (another iteration will pick up the next story).

## Important

- Work on ONE story per iteration
- Commit frequently
- Keep CI green
- Read the Codebase Patterns section in progress.txt before starting
